limitations: Constrained False/True token classification, not open-ended generation.
Confirmation uses plural variants of practice words; this is not a broad independent benchmark.
Two embedding/output rows change by about 39% in norm; untested tasks may regress.
The edit breaks the original 1-bit block structure in these rows; only the FP16 export was tested.
FP32 CPU computation was tested; the narrowest confirmation margin is about 0.0054.
Task activation caches are trusted host inputs, not independently authenticated by Wisp.
Wisp confirm replays the already-frozen host comparison; it is not a second independent holdout.
